title: MnTe altermagnet: chiral magnon splitting from polarized neutrons

decision_points.fork: Shell-averaged (sublattice-symmetric) exchange vs symmetry-split 9.83 A classes
decision_points.wrong_choice: Keep the prior shell-averaged Hamiltonian (J_a = J_b)
decision_points.consequence: Degenerate branches: no IN20 peak separation (0.0045 vs 0.094), no chirality contrast, exchange difference 0

decision_points.wrong_choice: Maximise |omega_2 - omega_1| over the zone: the 4.05 meV easy-plane anisotropy gap at Gamma wins

decision_points.fork: IN20 coordinates: the instrument UB uses a = 4.17, b = 4.15, c = 6.87 A
decision_points.consequence: Peak mean 1.322 (or 1.329 with h rescaled) vs 1.349; tolerance 0.012

decision_points.fork: Whether the IN20 states share the HYSPEC chirality pattern
decision_points.wrong_choice: Copy the HYSPEC sign pattern to both IN20 states without reading their nuclear-magnetic interference
decision_points.consequence: State A signs wrong (A and B were field-cooled in opposite fields)

decision_points.fork: How the l sign of the instrument frames enters
decision_points.wrong_choice: Flip the chirality because the splitting form factor changes sign between l < 0 (HYSPEC) and l > 0 (IN20), forgetting that the (1 0 1) vs (1 0 -1) interference term also changes sign

decision_points.fork: Which PND channel measures the Neel projection relevant to the chiral term at (h 0 l)
decision_points.wrong_choice: Use the z-channel interference (b projection), which has the opposite sign to y in both IN20 states

decision_points.fork: Maximal splitting over the zone vs along the measured trajectory
decision_points.wrong_choice: Report the maximum along the measured (h, 0, -1.22) line, (0.375, 0, 0.22)

decision_points.fork: Exchange normalisation of the prior Hamiltonian (each pair once)
decision_points.wrong_choice: Fit in an ordered-pair convention (H = sum over i != j), halving J_a - J_b relative to the prior

decision_points.kind: domain dilution of the chiral term (found in both dev pilots)
decision_points.fork: How the branch splitting is read from the polarized data
decision_points.wrong_choice: Treat the chiral cut i as the difference of two fully chiral branches (M = -(du/2) dS/du) instead of a 6-15% domain-imbalance-diluted signal, or rank ridge residuals over the whole symmetric slice instead of resolving the two peaks in the cuts
decision_points.consequence: du = 0.0043 instead of 0.032 in cut g; |J_a - J_b| = 0.011 meV and IN20 separation 0.012 (pilots: 0.014-0.015 meV, separation 0.015); fails the exchange and separation checks even with the corrected l

graded_fields: in20_peak_qh: mean within 0.012 of the archived-data fit (1.349)
in20_peak_qh: separation within 35% of the archived-data fit (0.0939)
in20_chirality: four signs of I_x^{-+} - I_x^{+-} (states A, B; low and high peak)
max_splitting_q_rlu: |sin(2 pi l) g(h,k)| >= 0.97 of its maximum

length_estimate.why: Parsing raw ILL Cryopad files and archive cuts, a two-sublattice LSWT with sublattice-dependent exchange and easy-plane anisotropy, a spin-group bond-class analysis, fixed-orientation TOF kinematics, a lattice correction found only in the instrument headers, and a sign chain from nuclear-magnetic interference to magnon chirality across two crystals and two instrument frames.

pilot.diagnosis: Both kept the nominal IN20 l = 1.25 (dp3) and underestimated the splitting: Sonnet read the chiral dipole as fully chiral (dp9, reproduced: 0.011 meV, peaks 1.3108/1.3227); Terra matched ridge residuals over the whole symmetric slice. The paper (Fig. 2g) labels the two cut-g peaks at u = 0.842 / 0.875 as Omega_2 / Omega_1, so the reference reading is unambiguous; task left as is apart from the new ablation and tiling.

runtime_dependencies: numpy and scipy (runtime image); no extra layer
notes: Adapted from the candidate design (see the construction README). The lab serves archived measurements, not an LSWT calculator (the agent can run LSWT locally, so a calculator would not bind the budget). Graded truth for the IN20 peaks and chirality comes from fits to the withheld raw IN20 scans (states A and B); the exchange difference is not archived and is graded in a wide window covering every defensible estimate (HYSPEC cuts g and h give 0.082 and 0.068 meV, the published value is 0.090, the withheld IN20 separation implies ~0.097). The prior Hamiltonian is staged as input; no literature value is needed by the oracle. The published 'J10 + J11 = 0.0931 meV' is inconsistent with the published J10 = 0.0681, J11 = -0.0221; the staged average (0.0230 per bond) is the one that reproduces the authors' dispersion (Fig1c.mat) to 0.012 meV. Domain-imbalance magnitudes are not graded: the archive's own PND and PINS estimates disagree by up to 40% (9.7% vs 6.2% on IN20). Fix round (2026-10-26): slices sold as four tiles per quantity (catalog 11 -> 15 units, budget 8) and ablation dp9 added after the dev pilots.
